summary: clampony preinstall fetches from Pastebin and anonymous paste host
details: clampony@1.0.9 declares `preinstall: node setup.js` in package.json. setup.js races fetches against https://pastebin.com/raw/z6K1Rg8J and https://calcal.ru/p/t5edjvR/raw using Promise.any, buffers the response, and writes it to a randomUUID() path under os.tmpdir(), then passes that filepath to a run() sink. The run() body is empty in this release, so the fetched bytes are staged but not executed in this exact version; the staging shape — preinstall lifecycle hook, mutable anonymous paste-host sources, tmpdir dropper path — is the standard install-time dropper pattern and both source URLs are attacker-mutable at any time. The package presents itself as a one-line clamp utility (index.js is 6 lines) with a name and description that mimic the well-known `clamp` helper, a cover-story shape for a typosquat delivery vehicle.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
